questions.q: Which α-amino acid is optically inactive?
questions.explain: Glycine (H₂N–CH₂–COOH) has two H atoms on the α-carbon, so it has no stereocentre; alanine is the simplest optically active one.

questions.q: Which amino acid is classified as basic?
questions.explain: Lysine has an extra NH₂ in its side chain, –(CH₂)₄NH₂. Asparagine is a trap: its side-chain nitrogen is an amide, so it is neutral.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an essential amino acid in the NCERT list?
questions.explain: Tyrosine is non-essential; the essential ten are valine, isoleucine, leucine, lysine, phenylalanine, methionine, threonine, tryptophan, histidine and arginine.

questions.q: A linear pentapeptide is formed from five amino acids. How many peptide bonds does it contain, and how many water molecules are lost in forming it?
questions.explain: n amino acids give n − 1 peptide bonds, and each –CO–NH– link forms with loss of one water molecule, so 4 bonds and 4 H₂O.
